answer: Each identity runs one relay in the meadow network and locks a 70-credit bond. A verifier sends pulse probes along its summit route; the relay must forward each probe intact and return a signed receipt. The first relay costs 36 credits, rising by 7 per extra relay from the same funder, so the kth costs 36+7(k-1) and the 1000th costs 7029; 1000 fakes pay 3,532,500 in fees plus 70,000 locked. A rented-relay ring fails because probes expose shared upstreams: shared delays and copied receipts slash each linked bond. An honest operator pays 36 once and reclaims the bond after a clean epoch.
